title: G08: Consolidate action, numerical and exporter semantic decisions
body:
# Centralize option, rate and capability decisions


## Maintainer GPU scope decision — 2026-11-13

GPU implementation and actual-device qualification are consolidated in #474,
separate from the current CPU release milestone. The maintainer has Apple Metal
hardware locally and no CUDA device or self-hosted NVIDIA runner. Metal and CUDA
require separate execution evidence; neither backend qualifies the other.
GPU requirements remain tracked and unqualified where evidence is missing, but
do not block this issue's CPU acceptance. Compile-only/fallback checks remain
useful and cannot count as device execution. See docs/DECISIONS.md item 17.

## Goal

Centralize option, rate and capability decisions. Complete the work and independent checks listed below for the first public BNG3 release.

## Decision

**[G08 / #178](https://github.com/RuleWorld/BNG3/issues/178): consolidation.** Put existing tools behind common interfaces and centralize option, rate and capability decisions. Reuse current abstractions rather than build a second framework.

## Current state

Audited `main` commit: `918a5fb1` (the full hash is in the evidence manifest). The implementation and validation entry points below exist and are the starting points for this work. Their presence is not a claim that all acceptance checks have run.

- `cpp/actions/ActionDispatch.cpp` (file present at `918a5fb1`)
- `cpp/engine/OdeIntegrator.cpp` (file present at `918a5fb1`)
- `cpp/engine/FiniteBackend.cpp` (file present at `918a5fb1`)
- `cpp/engine/BngsimAdapter.cpp` (file present at `918a5fb1`)

## Work

1. Inventory duplicated decisions in ActionDispatch, OdeIntegrator, exporters, FiniteBackend and BngsimAdapter.
2. Move them into existing compiled protocol/rate/backend interfaces with one owner per decision.
3. Keep backend-specific state separate and retain independent oracle cases through the refactor.

Additional work from #470:

1. Define compile-owned input, capability declaration, typed protocol, trajectory/session lifetime and common result/error metadata contracts.
2. Adapt native ODE/SSA/PLA/PSA, BNGsim, NFcore, NFnext, JAX and GPU paths through the same interface; provide a third-party registration contract.
3. Centralize options/rate/capability policy currently consumed by ActionDispatch, OdeIntegrator, exporters and adapters.

## Acceptance criteria

Check identities beginning `release-` below are new named CI acceptance jobs/cases to implement in the independent framework. Existing files above supply the starting implementation/harness. Scientific expected values come from pinned BNG2, native NFsim, PyBioNetGen, official SBML outputs or independent analytic/specification derivations as named; structural checks use the explicit architecture/schema/decision contract. Product-change agents do not author or alter their acceptance answers.

- [ ] `release-shared-decisions`: architecture checks identify one implementation per option/rate/capability rule.
- [ ] `release-interface-parity`: all backend and format consumers agree with independent expected semantics.
- [ ] `release-obligation-178`: each task above has its named check result, source/oracle identity and main commit recorded. For architectural/process work, compare the actual implementation/configuration with the recorded contract, including negative fixtures.

Additional acceptance criteria and inventory rows from #470:

- [ ] `release-backend-contract`: every backend accepts the same compiled input and returns the same result schema; invalid options fail consistently.
- [ ] `release-backend-oracles`: each backend passes assigned inventory cases against BNG2/native NFsim/analytic laws; actual GPU kernels and optional installs execute.

## Dependencies

#138, #140, #143, #144, #147

## Closing rule

Close when every acceptance item passes on `main`. Record the main commit and check artifacts. All maintainer decisions above are final; no further approval is needed.
